13.0.s.en: (4) The capture of Rabbah of Ammon

13.0.0.en: Absalom: the third son of David, born in Hebron; his mother's name was Maacah the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur. Tamar: the full sister of Absalom, whom Amnon, her half brother, raped.

13.0.1.en: The punishments with which David had been warned began to be fulfilled. The beginning of the painful events was Amnon's rape of his sister Tamar. Absalom the son of David had a beautiful sister whose name was Tamar, and Amnon, her half brother, felt a lustful passion toward her.

13.1.0.en: Vexed ... sick: he was distressed in spirit, and his heart became constricted and choked to the degree of physical illness.

13.1.2.en: Amnon's desire for Tamar was so pressing that it became an illness that took away from him the desire to engage in any activity, and he was at a loss how to reach what he sought, for Tamar was a virgin, and the customs of that age required that virgin girls live in a private dwelling, the house of the women, away from mixing with any of the men of the family; moreover, he could not marry her because she was his sister, and the Law forbids that. We wonder at Amnon's giving himself over to his lust for his sister, and perhaps his father David's sin with Bathsheba encouraged him to rush into this evil lust, for the sins of fathers can cause children to stumble and push them into evil.

13.2.0.en: Amnon had a cousin close to him, Jonadab the son of Shimeah, who is the same as “Shammah” mentioned in (1 Sam 16:9); the Scripture describes him as very wise). We shall see later that his wisdom was of the stumbling, evil kind.(

13.3.0.en: Jonadab noticed the leanness and weariness that Amnon was in, which increased day by day with no apparent cause, for he lived the life of the sons of kings and lacked nothing. So he asked him the reason, and he told him of his lust for Tamar: he felt that he loved her to the point of madness and could not restrain himself from her.

13.3.1.en: Satan is able to fabricate within a man or a woman an emotion toward another, and he justifies it as a need that a person cannot resist, in matters that are unlawful, that is, the love of a married man for another woman, or of a girl for a person who does not wish to marry her or where there are obstacles preventing it. So be watchful, my brother, because your enemy Satan has the power to persuade you and arouse you emotionally; do not give in to him as long as that is against the commandment... It is a fabricated feeling: resist it from the beginning and you will surely triumph by the grace of the Christ. And expose it to your father of confession and not to an evil friend, lest he lead you astray.

13.4.0.en: Jonadab gave him evil counsel to achieve his desire. He advised him to feign illness and lie on his bed, and his father would surely come to ask about him; then he should pretend to be sick and without appetite for food and ask his father to charge his sister Tamar to cook food for him with her own hands, so that perhaps his appetite would open and he would take to the food she prepared for him.

13.5.0.en: Amnon carried out the evil plan that his cousin had devised for him. He pretended to be ill, and the rest of the matters went as Jonadab had devised: the king came to ask about him, and Amnon asked him to allow his sister Tamar to come to him and cook food for him to eat from her hands.

13.6.0.en: David did not perceive any evil intention behind this request of Amnon, so he simply granted it and asked Tamar to go to Amnon's house to prepare food for him. If only David had prayed to God to rescue him and his children from evil! For prayer above all protects a person from many troubles, especially since a virgin sister's staying with her half brother was not a customary thing at that time.

13.7.0.en: The pan: a vessel in which cakes and food are prepared.

13.7.1.en: She emptied what she had prepared of food into a vessel and presented it to him, but he refused to eat in the presence of the servants and ordered everyone to go out, on the ground that he had no appetite in the presence of the servants, and perhaps he could eat quietly with his sister alone.

13.8.0.en: After the servants had gone out, Amnon asked Tamar to bring him the food while he was lying in his bed so that he might eat from her hand, and Tamar took the food she had prepared and brought it to Amnon's chamber.

13.9.0.en: She approached him in innocence and presented the food to him, but he did not take it from her; rather he seized her, asking her to lie with him and do evil.

13.10.0.en: Tamar was taken by surprise by this evil request, and she implored him not to harm her by assaulting her, telling him that the people of God are a holy people and do not commit such deeds, which are contrary to holiness, and she entreated him not to do this ugly deed to her.

13.11.0.en: Tamar went on, explaining that if she lost her purity she would lose her honor and shame would come upon her and she would not be able to face people. As for him, he would be in the eyes of all as one of the wicked and despised and would be rejected. And to find a way out of the situation, she asked him to put his wish to marry her to the king, who would grant him his wish (although the marriage of half brothers and sisters was forbidden by the Law (Lev 18:9), Tamar offered this idea hoping to escape the predicament so that the matter would be put before the king, who would do what he saw fit, and in this way she would rescue herself from this rape). Most likely she was in a remote chamber and could not cry out because no one would hear her; she was a pure woman, obedient to her father and humble, working with her own hands although she was a princess.

13.12.0.en: Despite Tamar's entreaties and her making him aware of the consequence of this deed, he did not heed her advice but overpowered her and obtained his wicked desire from her. This shows that there was a struggle and resistance on Tamar's part, but Amnon, by his bodily strength, was able to overcome his poor sister.

13.13.0.en: After he had obtained his desire, his love for her turned to intense hatred, greater than the love with which he had loved her, and his hatred for her overrode any human feelings, for he ordered her, in this state of grief and distress, to arise at once, leave the place and go far away. This shows the falseness of the lustful emotional feelings from which some suffer; rather, whoever is immersed in lust is a selfish, hard-hearted person who does not know love, because love is giving and not taking, and one who cannot control himself is a selfish person who deceives himself that he loves when he has not known true love.

13.14.0.en: Tamar said to him that there was no cause for his sending her away, for she had not been a cause of what had happened, and she explained to him that his sending her away was a greater evil than the evil he had done to her by his sin. But Amnon did not wish to listen to her in this either; rather his heart hardened and he increased in his evil to the point of ordering his servant to put her out and bolt the door after her. This shows the extent of his cruelty: he did not apologize to her for what he had done or have pity on her, for she had lost her virginity and was exposed to conceiving, and she had nothing with which to defend herself, especially since this expulsion took place immediately after the fall.

13.15.0.en: Tamar, like the other virgin princesses, wore a garment of many colors, showing that she was a virgin princess. The servant carried out his master's order and brought her outside and bolted the door after her.

13.15.1.en: (2) Absalom kills Amnon (vv. 19-29:) 19 And Tamar put ashes on her head, and rent her garment of divers colours that was on her, and laid her hand on her head, and went on crying. 20 And Absalom her brother said unto her, Hath Amnon thy brother been with thee? but hold now thy peace, my sister: he is thy brother; regard not this thing. So Tamar remained desolate in her brother Absalom's house. 21 But when king David heard of all these things, he was very wroth. 22 And Absalom spake unto his brother Amnon neither good nor bad: for Absalom hated Amnon, because he had forced his sister Tamar. 23 And it came to pass after two full years, that Absalom had sheepshearers in Baal-hazor, which is beside Ephraim: and Absalom invited all the king's sons. 24 And Absalom came to the king, and said, Behold now, thy servant hath sheepshearers; let the king, I beseech thee, and his servants go with thy servant. 25 And the king said to Absalom, Nay, my son, let us not all now go, lest we be chargeable unto thee. And he pressed him: howbeit he would not go, but blessed him. 26 Then said Absalom, If not, I pray thee, let my brother Amnon go with us. And the king said unto him, Why should he go with thee?

13.15.2.en: 27 But Absalom pressed him, that he let Amnon and all the king's sons go with him. 28 Now Absalom had commanded his servants, saying, Mark ye now when Amnon's heart is merry with wine, and when I say unto you, Smite Amnon; then kill him, fear not: have not I commanded you? be courageous, and be valiant. 29 And the servants of Absalom did unto Amnon as Absalom had commanded. Then all the king's sons arose, and every man gat him up upon his mule, and fled.

13.16.0.en: In expression of her intense grief at the loss of her honor, Tamar put dust on her head and tore the garment of many colors that she was wearing, which was a sign of the virginity she had lost, and she put her hand on her head as a sign of deep grief and of her awareness of the calamity that had befallen her (as women do to this day), and she began to cry out in a loud voice, lamenting her state and the misery she would suffer. She did all this as she was going to the house of her brother Absalom.

13.17.0.en: Regard not this thing: do not think much about this matter.

13.17.1.en: Remained desolate: depressed, withdrawn into herself.

13.17.2.en: Tamar reached Absalom's house, and he perceived, with his shrewdness and through her words crying out about the calamity that had struck her, and he asked her whether Amnon had assaulted her.

13.17.3.en: Absalom wanted to lighten the matter for his sister, so he asked her not to think much about what had happened and to leave the matter to him ... Tamar lived in the house of her brother Absalom, depressed and withdrawn into herself, meeting no one.

13.18.0.en: The news of what had happened reached David and he was greatly distressed, but he took no action against his son Amnon. This was another error on his part, like Eli the priest (1 Sam 4), and other calamities resulted from it, the details of which will come in later verses.

13.19.0.en: Absalom hated his brother Amnon in his heart, but he did not show his anger; he kept it within him until the right opportunity should come, when he would end his temporary silence and avenge himself and his sister.

13.20.0.en: Sheepshearers: those who shear the wool of the sheep.

13.20.1.en: Baal-hazor: its place is now “Jebel al-Qusur,” 4.5 miles northeast of Bethel and fifteen miles northeast of Jerusalem.

13.20.2.en: After two years the opportunity that Absalom had been waiting for to take his revenge came, for he was shearing his sheep, and the time of shearing sheep was considered a happy occasion on which feasts were held, because wool was a source of wealth, and Absalom invited his brothers to his feast.

13.20.3.en: Hatred and the desire for revenge remained hidden in Absalom's heart, and they led him to the sin of murder. The children of God must not allow anger to lodge in their hearts, lest it lead them to greater sins by which their lives are ruined. May you not go to sleep on any day before forgiving the one who has wronged you, so that God may forgive you your sins as you say in the Lord's Prayer; for if you do not forgive him, God will not forgive you. And if thoughts of resentment and anger against him fight you, pray earnestly to God to lift this war from you and strengthen your weakness.

13.21.0.en: Absalom went himself to invite his father the king and some of his men to his feast.

13.22.0.en: The king excused himself from going, he and his men, so as not to burden his son Absalom with special preparations to receive him, and despite Absalom's pressing, David did not wish to go, but he blessed him. This shows Absalom's cunning, for he made it appear a feast at which his father was supposed to be present, so that Amnon would not suspect anything.

13.23.0.en: Then Absalom asked the king to allow Amnon to go with him, as the heir to the throne, since he was the eldest of David's sons, so that he would attend on behalf of the king. At first the king saw no need for his son Amnon to go, because this too would cause Absalom trouble with special preparations, as a representative of the king. But in the face of Absalom's pressing, the king sent Amnon with him, and the rest of his brothers.

13.24.0.en: When Amnon's heart is merry with wine: when his consciousness is gone and he is carried away by intoxication from much wine. The opportunity that Absalom had planned for doing away with Amnon came, and he ordered his servants that when they saw that the wine had affected Amnon's consciousness, they were to kill him at once and fear nothing, for he was responsible for the killing and it was he who commanded them to do it, so they would bear no guilt; and he encouraged them and removed from them all fear or dread of attacking the heir to the throne. This shows the extent of Absalom's evil: he concealed the hatred in his heart for two years, which is a long time, in order to take revenge on his brother Amnon, and then how he persuaded his servants to kill Amnon and that they bore no responsibility, although his words were wrong and God would hold them to account for it, and the king too could punish them. For evil blinds a person's eyes and tries to deceive others.

13.25.0.en: The servants carried out Absalom's order and killed Amnon, and the rest of the brothers were terrified as they saw their eldest brother killed, so they mounted their mules and fled quickly from the place.

13.25.1.en: (3) David's grief and Absalom's flight (vv. 30-39:) 30 And it came to pass, while they were in the way, that tidings came to David, saying, Absalom hath slain all the king's sons, and there is not one of them left. 31 Then the king arose, and tare his garments, and lay on the earth; and all his servants stood by with their clothes rent. 32 And Jonadab, the son of Shimeah David's brother, answered and said, Let not my lord suppose that they have slain all the young men the king's sons; for Amnon only is dead: for by the appointment of Absalom this hath been determined from the day that he forced his sister Tamar. 33 Now therefore let not my lord the king take the thing to his heart, to think that all the king's sons are dead: for Amnon only is dead. 34 But Absalom fled. And the young man that kept the watch lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, there came much people by the hill side behind him. 35 And Jonadab said unto the king, Behold, the king's sons come: as thy servant said, so it is. 36 And it came to pass, as soon as he had made an end of speaking, that, behold, the king's sons came, and lifted up their voice and wept: and the king also and all his servants wept very sore. 37 But Absalom fled, and went to Talmai, the son of Ammihud, king of Geshur. And David mourned for his son every day. 38 So Absalom fled, and went to Geshur, and was there three years. 39 And the soul of king David longed to go forth unto Absalom: for he was comforted concerning Amnon, seeing he was dead.

13.26.0.en: The news reached David, but in an exaggerated form, for they told him that Absalom had killed all his sons, whereas Amnon alone had been killed. The king grieved greatly, tore his garments and lay on the ground, and all his men shared his grief and tore their garments, and this shows the signs of the intense grief into which the king and those with him fell.

13.26.1.en: We must not be carriers of every piece of news we hear without verifying its truth, for we may cause griefs or pains to others without real cause.

13.27.0.en: This hath been determined: he planned this matter.

13.27.1.en: Let not my lord the king take the thing to his heart: let the king not grieve this intense grief.

13.27.2.en: Jonadab was present with the king and was aware of the beginnings of the matters and of what had happened at the feast, for it was he who had advised Amnon of the plan to rape Tamar, so he tried to persuade the king that Amnon alone had been killed, and not the rest of his brothers, and that Absalom had been harboring evil against him since he assaulted his sister Tamar. This shows the extent of Jonadab's deceit: he is the source of the evil yet conceals his evil, and he is a type of Satan, who works in the hearts of people so that they become enemies to one another and then hides himself as though he had done nothing.

13.28.0.en: The young man that kept the watch: in ancient times kings appointed persons of keen sight to observe whether there were movements of enemies around the city.

13.28.1.en: After Absalom took his revenge and killed Amnon, he fled lest the king kill him. The watchman who observed any movements around the king's palace was performing his duty, and he saw a large number of people walking along the side of the mountain, and Jonadab said to the king, “Behold, the king's sons have come” alive from Absalom's feast, as I told you.

13.29.0.en: When Jonadab had made an end of speaking to the king, his sons arrived, and no sooner did they meet their father than they wept bitterly, and the king and all his men wept in grief for Amnon.

13.30.0.en: Geshur: it lies east of the Jordan River between Hermon and Bashan.

13.30.1.en: Absalom fled to his grandfather “Talmai,” king of Geshur, the father of his mother Maacah, to take refuge with him from the face of David his father. He welcomed him because he was his grandson, and he stayed with him for three years because he was in great fear of his father's punishment.

13.31.0.en: After a long period had passed since this event, David was comforted over the death of his son Amnon and longed to go himself to Geshur to bring Absalom back to his house, but he could not, because he knew that if he did this, people would accuse him of injustice among his sons and of laxity in applying the penalty of the Law to take the right of the slain son. This shows the tenderness of David's heart and his forgiveness and fatherly compassion.

13.31.1.en: If David resembled God in his compassion and forgiveness toward sinners, however great their evil, may you understand this so that you forgive others however great their evil, since God is so compassionate toward you.

13.31.2.en: David allows Absalom to return to Jerusalem
